Commentary.Commentary: A tricky period awaits the South Africans. There's still about 30 minutes of play left and with Wagner and Southee having a go with the new ball, they can make something happen. A wicket or two now and things could get really interesting. The Protea first innings is about to begin so don't go anywhere.

South Africa will be happy with how they've done, except for maybe leaking a few extra runs to the tail towards the end. The irony is that on the first day of a Test on a green track, the spinners took the bulk of the wickets, with Duminy taking 4 and Maharaj taking 2. Rabada and Morkel shared 2 apiece. Philander couldn't get any but was excellent with the ball as he kept things tight and ensured the pressure was never let off from his end.

New Zealand have been bowled out but they have a decent score on the board. Some handy cameos from Tim Southee and Jeetan Patel towards the end saw them post a total of 268. The top order didn't provide much resistance, except for some from Jeet Raval. He departed after a good fight but the real hero today for the Black Caps is Henry Nicholls. He scored his maiden ton and his heroics were instrumental in his side achieving this score. He first put up a solid 52-run stand with Jeet Raval and then an excellent 116-run stand with BJ Watling before he departed.

OUT! Duminy strikes! Tossed up in the line of the stumps, Wagner tries to clip it on the leg side but misses the ball completely. He gets rapped on the pads and the players appeal in unison. The umpire raises his finger in acceptance and Wagner is quick to use the final review. Replays show that there was no bat involved. Ball Tracker shows that the ball was pitched in line, impact in line and it's hitting. So that makes it three reds and Wagner has to walk back to the hut. NEW ZEALAND END ON 268.
Neil Wagner has been caught leg before and given out. He has decided to review the decision.
The batsman shows the full face of the bat and defends the ball off the back foot.
Floated outside off, Wagner cuts it through point for a couple.
The new ball is due in one over.
Dug in short, the batsmen ducks under it.
Way down the leg side, Patel stays in his crease undisturbed.
Yorker into the stumps, Patel somehow manages to block it away.
Neil Wagner is the last man in.

OUT! Southee's cameo comes to an end! Fuller delivery into the stumps, Southee goes for another biggie but this time does not get the desired contact. He gets the elevation but not the distance on it as Philander from mid on runs towards his right to take a fine catch.
Southee stays deep in his crease and defends it.
Length delivery into the stumps, Patel drives it through covers for a single.
FOUR! Top shot! Floated in the line of the stumps, Southee lofts it over the mid on region for a boundary.
Full into the stumps, Southee blocks it back to the bowler.
Length delivery outside off, Southee pushes it towards the fielder at covers.
SIX! Another biggie this time! Tossed up outside off, Southee gets to the pitch of the ball and smacks it over the long off region for a biggie.
SIX! Brilliant shot! Floated delivery just outside off, Southee dances down the track and smacks it over the long on boundary for a maximum.
Outside off, Southee tries to play at it but fails to make contact.
On the pads, Patel clips it towards the fielder at mid-wicket.
FOUR! Top shot! Angling into the pads, Patel slaps it through the leg gully region for a boundary.
Down the leg side, Southee clips it fine for a single.
Length delivery outside off, left alone.
Another short one for Southee, he goes for a pull but misses.
Short delivery into the body, Southee tries to play the upper cut but misses.
Floated outside off, Patel smacks it through the cover region for a couple.
Short delivery outside off, Patel smacks it through cover-point for a couple.
Outside off, left alone.
SIX! Gone the distance! Tossed up outside off, Patel dances down the track and smacks it over the long off region for a maximum.
Tossed up outside off, Southee lofts it over the point region for a single.
Floated outside off, Southee slashes his blade on it and gets an outside edge towards third man for a couple.
Short delivery into the body, Southee walks across and plays a pull shot towards fine leg and the batsmen run three runs.
FOUR! Sensational! Short delivery into the stumps, Southee pulls it through the mid-wicket region for a boundary.
Fuller delivery outside off, Southee lofts it over the extra-cover region for a couple.
Back of a length delivery down the leg side, Patel clips it fine down the leg side for a single.
Good length delivery outside off, the ball bounces a bit more and that catches Patel by surprise. He somehow manages to sway away from the line of the delivery.
Fuller length delivery outside off, Patel drives it straight towards the fielder at mid off.
Morne Morkel is called back into the attack.
Floated outside off, Southee covers his stumps and lets it through to the keeper.
Short delivery outside off, Southee slaps it towards mid off.
Quicker and flatter through the air outside off, left alone.
Tossed outside off, Patel cuts it towards point for a single.
Jeetan Patel will replace Watling in the middle.

OUT! BJ Watling is gone! A little unfortunate on his part, though. He kneels down to this flighted ball around off and attempts to sweep. Gets an inside edge which goes off the back pad and thuds into Quinton de Kock's gloves. South Africa appeal, the umpires aren't sure so the decision goes upstairs. Replays confirm that it indeed went off the back pad and not the ground. Watling has to make the long walk back.
The umpires have gone upstairs to check on a caught behind appeal against BJ Watling. The soft signal is not out. The South Africans seem confident though.
Outside off, it's run down to short third man for no run.
Beaten! Excellent length delivery just around off, moving touch a shade as the ball beats the outside edge of Tim Southee's bat.
Short of a length, defended away on the off side.
Philander brings out the short one and hits the deck hard, it's a little high for Southee so he doesn't flirt with that.
Fires it up there, attacks the stumps, Southee drives it towards the man at mid on.
Back of a length curling away from around off, a solid back foot defense is offered by Tim Southee.
Full delivery in the off stump channel, Watling drives it to the left of mid off and takes a single for doing so.
Tim Southee leaves it alone yet again and that brings us to the end of the over.
Way outside off again, left alone.
Wide, wide outside off. Once again JP drops it on a shorter length and it's left alone by the batsman.
Flat, short and outside off, Southee withdraws his bat and leaves it alone.
Full and wide outside off, some drift in the air on that occasion, Southee drives it straight to extra cover.
Tim Southee is the new man in.

OUT! Edged and gone! Good catch from Hashim Amla at first slip. Duminy bowls the straighter one outside off, Colin de Grandhomme steps out and fishes for it. Gets an edge which is taken well by Amla. Another wicket down for the home side.
Stays behind the line and leaves it alone.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Another leave. Shaping away, outside off, no shot offered.
Another tight leave from BJ Watling. Ensures that he's covered the line well and lets it go past him.
On the shorter side once more, Watling cuts it to the cover fielder.
Curling away on a back of a length, outside off and BJ Watling leaves it alone.
Vernon Philander is back on to bowl.
Looped up outside the line of off stump, it's driven nicely through the gap in the covers for two more.
Outside off on a fuller length, arms are shouldered by de Grandhomme.
Straightaway he attacks. Good, positive sign from Colin de Grandhomme. Loopy and full outside off, it's driven through to deep cover for a couple.
Colin de Grandhomme is the next man in to bat.

OUT! HE'S BOWLED 'EM! JP Duminy has dismissed Henry Nicholls but the southpaw has played a massive knock here today. Should be proud of the way he's steered his side to safer shores. It's tossed up on leg, turns a bit as Nicholls looks to flick it away. Brushes off the pads and crashes into the timber. Big breakthrough for South Africa, this. The wicket spells the end of a vital 116-run stand.
Pushed slightly quicker through the air, outside off, Henry comes out of his crease and keeps bat and pad close together while blocking it out.
Floats it up on a driving length around off, Watling steps out and wrists it down to long on for a run.
Wide outside off from Rabada, the left-hander goes after it wildly but misses.

FOUR! Two in two for Henry Nicholls. He hasn't put a foot wrong today. Patiently seen out the good one and punished the bad one. This is full on the stumps and it's driven back down past mid on for a boundary.
FOUR! Right off the middle of the bat. Lovely stroke. It's full and angling in on middle and leg, Henry Nicholls flicks it through mid-wicket for a boundary.
Length delivery aiming the top of off stump, Henry positions himself behind the line and deals with it comfortably.
Wide! Banged in short but it's too short, wide called by the umpire.
Fuller length ball on the stumps, blocked off the front foot.
From around the wicket, Rabada with a slightly fuller length, Nicholls shoulders his arms to it.
Allows the ball to come to him and turns it behind square on the leg side. Dot ball to end the over.
The batsman shows the full face of the bat and defends the ball off the back foot.
Flat, short and wide outside off, Watling doesn't need a second invitation to let that one be.
Outside off once more, played to point for nothing.
Outside off, it's turning in a long way as Watling looks to cut. Misses and it's collected by the keeper.
Short, flat and wide outside off, cut away square on the off side for a single.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Full outside off, it's driven through the covers. A superb effort from the fielder out in the deep saves a run for his side and keeps the batsmen down to three.
100-run stand between Henry Nicholls and BJ Watling.

FOUR! Another edge and it's flown away. Fortune is smiling down upon him today, isn't it? Back of a length outside off, Nicholls hangs his bat out and gets a healthy edge. It flies past a diving JP Duminy at gully and races away to the boundary line.
Maiden Test century for Henry Nicholls.

FOUR! Take a bow, Henry Nicholls! This is a fine, fine knock and he deserves every bit of it. He came at a time when his team was under pressure and has played an absolute beaut. Short and angling in, he swivels across and pulls it through the square leg region for a boundary. Brings up his century with that and removes his helmet to acknowledge the cheers all around. Beautiful stuff!
On a bit of a fuller length outside off, left alone.

FOUR! This may well be Henry Nicholls' day. There are two slips and a gully in place and he bisects the gap perfectly, even if it unintentionally. Full and outside off from around the wicket, Nicholls throws his bat at it and gets it off the outer half between the slip cordon and gully aerially. Races away to the fence for a boundary.
Outside off, flat ball to Watling, no prizes for guessing what he does! He leaves it alone.
A bit of flight on this occasion, draws Watling forward. He reaches out to it and drives it straight to the cover fielder.
Full and flat outside off, left alone.
Full on the stumps, it's comfortably eased towards mid-wicket for a single.
Flat, short and turning in around off, Watling goes back and nudges it to backward square leg for one.
From around the wicket, fuller and flat darted outside off, Nicholls comes down the track and pushes it to cover-point with the full face of the bat for a single.
Similar delivery like the previous one, same result. Left alone to end the over.
Bangs this in on a shorter length but it's well outside off, not going to trouble someone like BJ Watling who leaves it alone.
Outside off, a good length delivery from Rabada, no shot offered by BJ Watling.
Slanting away on a good length, on off, it's dabbed away to point for nothing.

We're entering the fag end of the day and all of a sudden Kagiso Rabada is making the ball talk. On a bit of a back of a length, goes past the batsman and moves heavily as it thuds into de Kock's gloves.
Rabada from around the wicket hurls a fuller length ball and gets it to angle in on the pads, Nicholls flicks it through mid-wicket and gets three runs for it. Moves into the 90s with that.
Further outside off, on a shorter length, it's left alone.
Flat and short outside off, Watling plays inside the line but is beaten past the outside edge.
Turning in on middle and off, turned to the on side for an easy single.
Loopy ball on a driving length outside off, Nicholls comes forward and blocks.
Turning in on a flatter trajectory, catches Henry on the thigh pad as he attempts to play off the back foot.
Flat, short and quick outside off, looks to cut Nicholls but misses it completely.
Shouts for a leg before but it's going down leg, so the umpire turns it down quickly. Spears it in full on middle and leg, catches Watling low on the pads as he looks to flick.
Outside off on a good length, Watling lets it be as he watches the ball go past him.
Short and going down leg, BJ crouches quite low and lets the ball sail over his head.
Full and angling in on the stumps, straightens up and even starts moving away somewhat, BJ Watling pushes it back to Rabada with a straight blade.
Good length delivery outside off, arms are shouldered to this one.

Good delivery to start the over with. Just enough movement, bowling in good rhythm as well. Bowls it on a back of a length around off, it straightens up nicely as Watling looks to have a little poke at it. Is beaten and collected by Quinton de Kock behind the stumps.
Tossed down the leg side, Watling clips it through the mid on region for a single.
Outside off, Watling pushes it towards the fielder at point.
Short and around off, Nicholls cuts it through the cover region for a single.
Floated outside off, Watling walks across and clips it through mid-wicket for a single.
Tossed outside off, Watling stays in his crease and pushes it back to the bowler.
Full on the pads, Nicholls gets an inside edge onto his pads which runs down towards short third man for a single.
JP Duminy is called back into the attack.
Outside off on a back of a length, it's left alone by BJ Watling.
FOUR! Lovely timing. It's pitched slightly ahead of a length, outside off, Watling leans into it and beautifully drives it through the covers for a boundary.
Outside off on a good length, looks to go after it but misses.

There's a big inside there, almost dragged it back on. Rabada gets it to come back in sharply as Watling tries to put bat on ball. Is cramped for room and ends up getting an inside edge past the leg stump. It goes down to fine leg as the batsmen take a couple of runs.
Outside off on a good length, it's let through for the keeper to collect.

Play and a miss from BJ Watling! It's on a back of a length, outside off with a bit of width, he goes after it with a punch as he looks to carve the off side. Fails to make any connection and it goes behind to the keeper.
Flat and short around off, Nicholls stays back and keeps it out.
Loopy and fullish in length, around off, a solid front foot defensive shot presented by the batsman.
FOUR! Full toss outside off, Henry positions himself quickly and smacks it through the line for a boundary. Pierced the gap in the covers to perfection as he gets himself another boundary.
Fullish in length and pitched well outside off, it's turning in but Henry pads it away easily.
Loopy ball outside off, Nicholls gives the charge and hits it straight back to the bowler.
Darts this fuller on middle and leg, it's coming in with the angle as Watling goes back and flicks it through backward square leg. Kept a bit low as well so BJ did well to bring his bat down in time.
Maintains it on the shorter side of things, it's defended off the back foot.
Jagging back in on middle and leg, raps Nicholls high on the thigh pad as he attempts to play at it. Stifled shouts all around but nothing much to it.
Way, way outside off, no-brainer for Henry Nicholls to not have anything to do with that.
Shaping away once again, easy leave for Henry here.
Tighter line from Rabada, keeps it very close to the off stump as he bowls it on a back of a length, it's kept out off the back foot by the southpaw.
Slanting away from the left-hander on a back of a length, outside off, Henry Nicholls leaves it alone.
The batsman rocks onto the back foot and punches the ball. One run added to the total.
Watling dances down the track and pushes it to extra cover. Wants the single and there's a shy at the striker's end which misses. The run is completed.
Works this one towards mid-wicket but for no run.
Goes on the back foot and works it through backward square leg for a single.
Flat and short around off, Nicholls off the back foot plays it back down the track.
Loopy delivery well outside off, blocked off the front foot by reaching out.
Back of a length delivery short into the body, Watling defends it towards square leg.
Sprayed short down the leg side, Nicholls pulls it on the leg side for a single.
On the pads, Nicholls works it square of the wicket on the leg side.
Length delivery outside off, left alone.
Back of a length delivery, Nicholls stands tall and pushes it on the off side.
Good length delivery angling into the stumps, Henry stays in his crease and defends it well.
Another solid defensive shot from BJ Watling and that will be the end of the over.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Full on the stumps, it swept through square leg for a single.
FOUR! Attacking stuff from Henry Nicholls. The southpaw skips out, gets to the pitch and and swings it across the line through mid-wicket for a one bounced boundary.
Stays right behind the line and works it on the on side.
Floats it just back of a driving length, Nicholls dances down and hits it back to the bowler.
So the final session of play is underway. Henry Nicholls and BJ Watling will continue with the bat for New Zealand. Keshav Maharaj will start with the ball for South Africa.
... DAY 1, SESSION 3 ...

Good recovery from New Zealand. Scored 87 runs and the only wicket to fall in the entire session was of Jimmy Neesham's, who got out to Keshav Maharaj after getting off to a positive start. Henry Nicholls and BJ Watling have done an exceptional job to shore things up with an unbeaten 59-run partnership. They've done well so far and need to continue the same in the final session, as a wicket could change things for them completely. South Africa will be aiming for that breakthrough early in the session and take things from there. The final session of the day will begin shortly. Stay tuned.
Length delivery to end the session, Watling drives it elegantly down the ground through the mid off region for a couple. That's TEA ON DAY 1!
Length delivery around off, Watling prods forward in defence.
The batsman chooses to leave the ball outside his off stump.
Short delivery outside off, Watling shuffles across and defends it.
Length delivery into the stumps, Watling covers his stumps and blocks the ball well.
Angling into the stumps from a good length, Watling stays deep in his crease to defend it.
Floated outside off, Nicholls reaches the pitch of the ball and defends it.
Watling dances down the track and drives it through mid off for a single.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Outside off, Watling prods forward in defence.
Floated outside off, Henry dances down the track and elegantly drives it down the ground. The fielder from mid off dives to save a certain boundary and the batsmen only manage to take a run.
Floated in the line of the stumps, Nicholls shuffles across and clips it towards the fielder at mid-wicket.
Full delivery nipping back in, Watling gets an inside edge onto his pads.
Good length delivery outside off, left alone.
FOUR! Class act! Full and wide outside off, Watling leans into the drive and plays it through the extra cover region for a boundary.
50-run stand between Nicholls and Watling!
Sprayed down the leg side, Nicholls clips it through the square leg region for a triple.
Fuller outside off, Nicholls drives it straight to the fielder at mid off. Rabada makes a mess there as he lets the ball run through between his legs for a couple.
Dug in short down the leg side, Nicholls ducks under it.
Down the leg side, Watling clips it towards the fielder at mid on.
Floated outside off, Watling drives it straight to the fielder at mid off.
Watling prods forward and defends it.
Flighted down the leg side, Watling reaches to the pitch of the ball and drives it straight towards the fielder at covers.
Tossed up around off, Watling pushes this one towards mid off.
Floated around off, Watling camps back and pushes it back to the bowler.
Sprayed down the leg side, Watling clips it down the leg side for a single.
Length delivery outside off, Nicholls finds an outside edge towards the third man region for a single.
Angling across from a length outside off, Nicholls shoulders his arms to it.
Angling across from a length outside off, left alone.
Full into the stumps, Nicholls pushes it towards the fielder at mid on.
Good length delivery angling across, Nicholls stays deep in his crease and defends it towards mid on.
Tossed up in the line of the stumps, Watling goes for the sweep but misses it completely.
Tossed up around off, Watling stays in his crease and defends it.
Watling prods forward and defends it.
Full outside off, Watling drives it straight to the fielder at covers.
Watling gets behind the line of the ball to defend it.
Tossed up outside off, Watling prods forward and defends it.
Angling down the leg side, Watling clips it through mid-wicket for a single.
Good length delivery which nips in a bit late after pitching, Watling tries to push at it but the ball sneaks in between the bat and the body.
Angling into the pads, Watling fails to clip it on the leg side and he gets hit on the pads.
Dug in short outside off, Watling ducks under it.
The batsman has played it towards mid-wicket. One run added to the total.
Angling across from a length outside off, Nicholls shoulders his arms to it.
Full outside off, Watling drives it straight to the fielder at covers.
Tossed up outside off, Nicholls sweeps it towards square leg for a single.
Full outside off, Watling lunges forward and paddle scoops it towards fine leg for a single.
Darting in the line of the stumps, Watling prods forward and defends it.
Tossed up outside off, HN drives it through covers for a single.
Full outside off, Nicholls drives it towards the fielder at covers.
Short delivery into the body, Watling uses his crease, stands tall and defends it back to the ground.
Good length delivery outside off, left alone.
Nicholls clips it on the leg side with soft hands and calls his partner for a quick single.
Back of a length delivery around off, Nicholls defends it towards the point region.
Angling across from a good length, Nicholls covers his stumps and lets it through to the keeper.
Back of a length delivery outside off, Nicholls camps back and defends it.
Morne Morkel is back on to bowl again.
Tossed up outside off, Watling gets behind the line of the delivery to defend it.
Floated up in the line of the stumps, Nicholls sweeps it through the square leg region for a single.
On the pads, Watling clips it through mid on for a single.

How did that not hit the stumps? Floated outside off, Watling lunges forward in defence, gets an inside edge onto his tracks. The ball then goes onto hit his triceps and ricochets towards the stumps. Watling rushes back to stop the ball but it had already crossed the stumps.
Watling prods forward and defends it.
Floated outside off, Nicholls dabs it through point for a single.
FOUR! Top shot! Good length delivery outside off, Watling waits for it and punches it through covers for a boundary.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Back of a length delivery, Watling uses his crease and pushes it back to the bowler.
Watling stays deep in his crease and defends it well.
Angling into the pads. Watling goes for the flick but misses and the ball raps him on his pads.
Watling stays in his crease and clips it towards the fielder at square leg.

FOUR! First boundary after drinks! Floated outside off, Nicholls goes to cut it late through the off side but ends up getting it off the outer half of the bat. The ball races away towards the boundary past the slip fielder.
Floated around off, Nicholls prods forward and defends it.
Spinning in from outside off, Nicholls stays deep in his crease and pushes it back to the bowler.
Tossed up in the line of the stumps, Watling paddles it fine down the leg side for a single.
Floated outside off, BJ Watling drives this one straight to the fielder at mid off.
Fuller outside off, Nicholls blocks it away towards mid off and rushes for a quick single. Good running between the wickets there.
Good length delivery outside off, Watling shoulders his arms to it.
Back of a length delivery around off, BJ gets behind the line of the delivery and defends it well. The crisis man has his defence very well in check.
Fuller delivery outside off, which nips away after pitching. Watling prods forward and lets it through to the keeper.
Back of a length delivery outside off, Watling shuffles across, stands tall and defends it well.
Fuller delivery outside off, Watling dabs it towards the fielder at point.
Angling in from a length outside off, Watling stays in his crease and defends it.
Floated outside off, Nicholls gets behind the line of the delivery to defend it.
Tossed up outside off again, Watling dances down the track and drives it through mid off for a single.
Floated outside off, HN  runs it down towards third man for a single.
Tossed up in the line of the stumps, Henry sweeps it towards the fielder at square leg.
Again tossed up outside off, Nicholls pads it away.
Floated outside off, Nicholls drives it straight to the fielder at covers.
Another full delivery around off, Watling kills the movement by reaching the pitch of the ball. He manages to block it away.
Watling prods forward and pushes the full length ball back to the bowler.
Angling in from a good length, Watling defends it towards the fielder at covers.
Length delivery just outside off, the ball nips away after pitching. Watling stays in his crease and tries to poke at it but luckily fails to make contact.
The batsman shoulders arms to let that one through.
Good length delivery outside off, Watling pushes it towards the fielder at covers.
Time for Drinks.
Shorter in length and on a flatter trajectory, Henry Nicholls goes deep inside his crease and deals with it out safely.
Another successful padding attempt. A battle of patience here. Interesting to see who breaks first.
This time manages to connect the front pad. Gets it away on the off side.
An exact replica of the first delivery. Dot ball.
Stays back to the flat ball and keeps it down on the track.
Full and flat wide outside off, Henry attempts to pad it away but it goes past his front leg.
Shortish around off, a back foot punch from BJ Watling and that's the end the over.
Just ahead of a length, around off, blocked away on the off side off the front foot.
Length delivery aiming the top of off stump, Watling with a solid defense from within his crease.

There was a lot of swing for Philander there. That one moved away a loooooonnnng way. Length delivery angling in on off, it seams away after pitching and beats the outside edge. Beats the off stick as well and keeps on moving away as Quinton de Kock behind the stumps collects it.
Length delivery on middle and leg, Nicholls pushes it in front of mid on and takes a quick single.
Hurls a length delivery in the channel outside off, Henry Nicholls ensures he has his off stump covered and makes a leave to it.
Vernon Philander is back into the bowling attack.
Watling is rock solid in defense. It's drifting in to him on a fullish length, he meets it with a straight bat.
Has a change of angle and comes from around the wicket, floats it on off, blocked.
Darted full and it's pushed quicker through the air, swept through to deep square leg for a run.
Flatter and shorter outside off, punched away a bit square on the off side for no run.
Good use of the feet there. Nicholls skips down and blocks.
Flatter, shorter and straighter outside off, Henry covers the line well and lets it be.
At 132 kph, Kagiso spears it fuller on off stump, BJ Watling presses ahead and buries it into the track to end the over.
Great carry on that occasion for Rabada. He hurls it on a back of a length outside off, it's left alone. Harmless really.
Fractionally ahead of a length, outside off, Watling prods forward and shoulders his arms.
Over the wicket, just outside off on a good length, BJ with a watchful leave.
Just back of a length, coming back in on leg, Nicholls hops across and nurdles it just wide of the mid-wicket fielder for a single.
From around the wicket, it's banged in short and angling down, ducked and evaded by Henry Nicholls.
FOUR! Great way to get off the mark. Brings out the broom and sweeps it through backward square leg for a boundary.
The batsman rocks onto the back foot and punches the ball.
Gives this some decent air and bowls it fuller around off, defended off the front foot.
Some nice drift into the batsman as Maharaj comes from a little wide of the crease, Watling pushes it away on the off side.
Around the wicket now, floats it up on off, Watling leans across and flicks it to mid-wicket for nothing.
Full on middle and leg, driven towards mid on for one.
Just about caught the edge. Rabada bowling an excellent line. Hurls in the channel outside off, almost draws the edge too. Lovely bowling.
Length ball outside off, some width on offer as Watling plays it to the left of the cover fielder.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Moving away a shade from around off, on a good length, it's not played at by the batsman.
Outside off, with a slightly opened face BJ Watling dabs it to the point region.
Length delivery shooting off the surface around off, Watling defends it out from within his crease.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Not much turn on this occasion, it's outside off, left alone.
5th Test fifty for Henry Nicholls!
FOUR! What a way to bring up the milestone. Stylish from Henry Nicholls. It's tossed up, he sees the flight and lofts it back over the bowler's head for a boundary.
Keshav Maharaj is keeping the pressure on the Kiwi batsmen by bowling probing lengths. Can the duo of Nicholls and Watling stitch in a partnership to steady the ship for the hosts?
Another front foot defense from the southpaw to keep it out.
Tossed up from Maharaj, it's blocked off the front foot and into the track.
FOUR! Wonderful timing. Full on the stumps, Nicholls walks across a step, kneels down and sweeps it through backward square leg. Beats the man in the deep as the ball rolls away across the rope.
From over the wicket to Watling, he doesn't bother playing at it.
Back of a length outside off, Henry drops it in front of covers and scurries to the other end to complete the run.
Length delivery outside off, another leave from the southpaw.
Serves this outside off, bowls it just ahead of a length, arms are shouldered to this one.
Angling in on middle and off, Nicholls uses the angle and clips it behind square on the leg side.
FOUR! Full toss on off, Nicholls just drives this back down through mid off and sends it across the rope for a boundary.
Floats it up on off, Watling with a solid front foot defense.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
BJ Watling is the next man in.

OUT! Maharaj with another breakthrough! The positive start from Jimmy Neesham comes to an end. Flighted around off, Neesham comes ahead to block but in the process, drags his back leg out. Quinton de Kock sees this and he's lightning with his glovework. Whips the bails off in an instant and his face says he's got his man. Neesham starts walking without even waiting for the decision and replays show why. He's clearly out. Another wicket down for the Kiwis. They're in real trouble here.
A stumping appeal against Jimmy Neesham is referred upstairs by the umpire. The southpaw has started walking back. He, like de Kock, thinks he's gone.
Flat delivery around off, punched off the back foot to covers.
Flat, short and outside off, Jimmy goes back and punches it back down the ground to mid off.
Brilliant fielder from Rabada, he is a good athlete. Tossed up on middle and leg, Neesham sweeps it towards backward square leg where Rabada makes a good low dive to his right to stop it.
Keshav Maharaj is brought back into the attack.
Short and angling down leg, it's ducked and evaded by the batsman.
Well outside off, pitched just back of a length, it's left alone.
Walks across to this length ball and nudges it away on the on side.

Rabada almost gets his man! The short ball comes into play and almost does him in. Bumper on off, shoots off the deck a bit, rises onto Nicholls who awkwardly fends it away on the off side. Was in the air for a while but fell well short of Bavuma who came running in from point.
Fires this fuller in length, it's driven to mid on.
From around the wicket, Rabada bangs it on a back of a length, gets it to angle in from around off, Henry Nicholls walks across, gets behind the line and defends it down into the track.
FOUR! Too full this time from Morkel and it's punished. On the stumps, it's driven back down past mid on for a boundary. Solid way to end the over.

Ooofff... Close! Stays too deep inside the crease and almost pays the price for it. Fuller and going away from around off, Jimmy Neesham doesn't come as forward as he should as he attempts to defend. It goes just past the edge and the off stump behind.
FOUR! BANG! That's a good shot. Neesham pounced on the short ball in a flash and slammed the pull through mid-wicket. Gets a boundary to his name.
Morkel needs to get the line right, seems to be having some trouble getting his radar right. Bowls it on the hips, it goes off the body and on the leg side as the batsmen take a leg bye.
Taling back in on middle and leg, it's a big too straight as Neesham picks it off his pads and works it behind square on the leg side for a run.
FOUR! Back of a length delivery just around off, Neesham looks to defend off his back foot and gets an edge past the third slip fielder. Races away to the third man fence for a boundary.
Full ball on the stumps, it's driven back down the track to end the over.
The batsman shows the full face of the bat and defends the ball off the back foot.
Moving away off the deck, on a length, Henry has nothing to do with it.
Pounds this on a back of a length, outside off, Nicholls hangs back and defends it off the back foot.
Length delivery outside off, left alone for the keeper to collect.
Back of a length delivery angling into the body, worked behind square on the leg side for a single.

FOUR! Edged and away! Not that risky if you actually look at it. Used the pace well and let it fly. It was short and around off, he just threw his bat at it and got it over the slip cordon. It was a little close to his body but he managed to get it away.
The batsman shows the full face of the bat and defends the ball off the back foot.
Good length delivery on off, angling in from around off, Henry Nicholls gets an inside edge past the leg stump as he looks to defend.

FOUR! Shot! The width was there and Nicholls had a go at it. Short and outside off, he flashes his bat at it and cuts it aerially through the gap between gully and the slip cordon. It races away to the third man fence for a boundary.
Comes from around the wicket and angles in a back of a length delivery into the hips, Jimmy Neesham hops across and tucks it past the backward square leg fielder for a single.
Length ball on leg, Nicholls picks it off his pads and clips it through the gap in the mid-wicket region for three runs. Lovely placement on that occasion.
Morne Morkel to bowl from the other end.
Good length ball from Rabada, it's left alone to end the over.
Beaten! Beauty from Rabada. Length delivery nipping away, around off, Jimmy Neesham hangs back to block but the ball goes past the outside edge.
On the shorter side of the length, just outside off, blocked once more by staying behind.
Back of a length delivery slanting across, it's kept out off the back foot.

Well, well, well... That was close. Much to Rabada's dismay, that didn't come back in enough. Length delivery around off, comes back in a bit as Neesham shuffles across to leave it alone. It brushes off his pads and thuds into de Kock's gloves.
Bit too straight as it's on the pads, Henry Nicholls flicks it away behind square on the leg side for a single.
Kagiso Rabada to take the ball now. Three slips and a gully in place.
Turning in from a good length, around off, Neesham goes back and works it down in front of short leg.
Tossed up outside off, it's left alone by Neesham.

We are back for the second session of play. Henry Nicholls will continue with Jimmy Neesham now partnering him in the middle. A lot rides on these two as not many batsmen are left for NZ. Keshav Maharaj to finish his remaining over...
... DAY 1, SESSION 2 ...

Got to feel for Jeet Raval, did all the hard work to lead the fightback and get his side into a decent position, but got out just before the break. With 4 wickets down and a soft New Zealand lower middle order to aim at, South Africa will be eager to get back out there quickly. The Kiwis have a tough task in the afternoon session. Join us in a short while.

One moment can change the complexion of the entire game, and that's exactly what's happened here. Just at the brink of lunch, Keshav Maharaj has picked up a wicket to put his side back in the driver's seat. Heartbreaking for New Zealand, really. They were motoring along at a steady rate with Jeet Raval and Henry Nicholls looking solid. They stitched 52 runs between them before the former departed.

OUT! Maharaj gets his man! Floated outside off, Raval lunges forward in defence. Gets an outside edge which flies away towards Hashim Amla at first slip who does not make any mistake and pouches a simple catch. All the efforts of batting out the whole session go in vain as Raval makes his way back to the pavilion. With the wicket, the umpires call for LUNCH ON DAY 1.
Full just outside off, Raval tries to block it but is beaten by the extra pace there.
Tossed up outside off, Raval covers his stumps and lets it through to the keeper.
50-run stand between Raval and Nicholls!

FOUR! Nearly got his man on the first ball! Edged! Floated outside off, Raval goes to drive at it but manages to find a thick outside edge which flies through the vacant second slip region. Hashim Amla at first slip dived towards his left but could not reach it as the ball raced away to the boundary.
Keshav Maharaj is on to roll his arm. This will be the last over before lunch. Can he make something happen?
Length delivery just outside off, Nicholls manages to find an inside edge into his pads.
FOUR! Good shot! Full delivery outside off, Nicholls drives it through the cover region for a boundary. The fielder gives it a chase but the ball won the race.
Fuller delivery into the stumps, Raval clips it through the mid-wicket region for a single. Calls for a second but Nicholls sends him back in time.
Philander is seen bringing on some more sawdust to put down on the landing area. Probably slipping somewhat as he's steaming in to bowl.
Fuller delivery outside off, Raval opens his face of the bat and guides it towards the fielder at second slip.
Good length delivery outside off, Raval is untested there.
Angles this one into the stumps from a length, Nicholls defends it on the leg side with soft hands and rushes to complete a quick single. Quick running from the batsmen.
Tossed up outside off, Raval prods forward and defends it.
Short and wide outside off, Nicholls punches it through covers for a single.
Fires this one again in the line of the stumps, Nicholls defends it back to the bowler.
Down the leg side this time by Duminy, Nicholls clips it towards the fielder at mid-wicket.
Full in the block hole, Henry blocks it away towards covers.
Full into the stumps, Nicholls drives it towards mid on.
Another leave from Raval. It's been long since he last played a delivery outside off.
Brave leave from Raval! Good length delivery which nips in a bit after pitching, Raval lets it through to the keeper.
Angling into the stumps, Raval gets behind the line of the ball and pushes it back to the bowler.
Good length delivery outside off, Raval covers his stumps and shoulders his arms to it.
Angling into the stumps, Raval gets behind the line of the delivery to defend it.
Short delivery into the body, Raval pulls it towards the fielder at mid-wicket. Luckily he managed to keep it along the ground.
Down the leg side, HN gets behind the line of the ball to defend it.
Floated in the line of the stumps, Nicholls lunges forward and defends it.
A bit short this time, Henry jags back and punches it towards the fielder at point.
Again flatter through the air outside off, Nicholls pushes it towards the fielder at point.
Tossed outside off, Nicholls prods forward and defends it.
Fires this one into the stumps, the batsman is caught by surprise as he just manages to block it away.
Some spin for South Africa as JP Duminy is brought on to have a go with the ball. Faf probably wants to vary things up a bit just before the lunch break.
Length delivery angling in from outside off, Raval shoulders his arms to let that one through.
Full delivery outside off, Raval stretches out towards it and lets it through to the keeper.
Another one sprayed down the leg side, Raval flicks it towards the fielder at square leg. Another dot ball.
Back of a length delivery down the leg side, Raval clips it towards the fielder at mid-wicket.
Raval covers his stumps and lets the angling ball through to the keeper.
What a delivery to start his second spell with! Bowls it on a length outside off, the ball nips in and nearly kisses the off pole. Brave leave by Raval.
Vernon Philander returns to the attack.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.

In the air...short! Bowls it on a length outside off, Nicholls tries to play at it and gets a thick outside edge which falls just short of JP Duminy at backward point who cannot stop it. The ball runs away for a couple behind him.
Dug in short into the body, Nicholls ducks under it.
Length delivery angling into the stumps, Nicholls gets behind the line of the delivery to defend it.
FOUR! Beautiful! Angling in from a length outside off, Nicholls leans into it and drives it crisply through the cover region for a boundary.
Length delivery outside off, Nicholls shoulders his arms at it.
Good length delivery which nips away after pitching, left alone.
Fourth leave in a row. Rabada bowls it outside off, Raval covers his stumps and lets it through.
Another delivery outside off, Raval is undisturbed by the line of the delivery.
Another length delivery outside off, Raval covers his stumps and lets it through to the keeper. Rabada will need to make the batsman play a bit more.
Good length delivery outside off, Raval shoulders his arms to it.
Sprayed down the leg side to start with, Nicholls clips it fine down the leg side for a single.
Angling into the pads, Nicholls makes the most of it and clips it through the fine leg region for a triple. So he will keep strike.
Length delivery outside off, Nicholls gets a thick outside edge through the gully region for a couple.
How did he survive that? Length delivery angling in, Nicholls stays in his crease and tries to play at it but he is beaten by the away movement totally. Lucky not to edge it.
Dug in short this time by Morkel, Nicholls sways away from the line of the delivery.
Length delivery angling into the stumps, Nicholls prods forward in defense and gets an inside edge into his pads.
Angling into the pads, Nicholls tries to clip it on the leg side but fails to make contact. The ball hits him high on the thigh pads.
Another back of a length delivery into the stumps, Raval stays deep in his crease to defend it.
Raval stands in his crease and clips it on the leg side.
Nearly got to the fielder! Short delivery into the body, Raval defends it in front off the fielder at short leg.
The short ball is not doing the trick for Rabada. Bowls another short ball into the body, Raval defends it from within the crease.
Short delivery into the body, Raval camps back and defends it well.

On a length outside off, Raval stays in his crease and pushes it towards covers for a quick single. Bavuma the fielder there, quickly reaches to it, gathers the ball and throws it on the non-striker's end. Misses and the ball runs away for an overthrow. Two runs take in total.
Length delivery outside off, HN punches it towards the fielder at point.
Another short one into the body, Nicholls stands tall in his crease and defends it off the back foot.
Length delivery angling in this time, Nicholls gets behind the line of the delivery to defend it.
Good length delivery outside off, which nips away after pitching. Nicholls shoulders his arms to it.

Back of a length delivery into the body, Nicholls stays deep in his crease and tries to defend it. Cannot get his bat in time as he gets hit on his ribs. That might have hurt. Shows no signs of pain though.
Length delivery outside off, left alone this time.
FOUR! Top shot! Length delivery outside off, Raval leans forward and drives it firmly down the ground through the mid off region for a boundary.
On a length angling across, Raval goes fetching for it but he was totally beaten by the away movement.
FOUR! Good shot! Full in the line of the stumps, Raval drives this crisply through the mid on region for a boundary. Gets another one to his name.
Angling across from a length way outside off, Raval is untroubled as it is harmless throughout.
Length delivery in the line of the stumps, Raval waits for the delivery and defends it well.
Short delivery down the leg side, Raval ducks under it.

Full delivery and Raval won't miss out on those. He just stands in his crease to elegantly drive it through covers. The ball does not reach the fence but the batsmen manage to pick up three good runs.

The change of angle almost doing the trick, took Raval totally by surprise. Angles it in from a length which nips away after pitching. Raval tries to play it in line of the ball but is totally beaten by the away movement.
Comes around the wicket this time, fires this one in the line of the stumps. Raval covers his timber and pushes it towards mid on.
Full outside off, Raval drives it towards the fielder at covers. Cannot find the gap this time.
Length delivery outside off, Raval punches it over the point fielder for a couple.
Full outside off, Nicholls drives it through the cover region for a triple.
Morne Morkel is back into the attack.
Another leave by Raval this time to end the over.
Angling across from a length, left alone.
Good length delivery angling away this time, Raval hangs his bat in the middle but fails to make contact.
Again on the leg side, Raval defends it in front of the fielder at short leg.
Down the leg side, Raval tries to clip this one but fails to make contact.

NOT OUT! Length delivery, angling into the pads. Raval tries to push this one on the leg side but is totally beaten by the inward movement and is rapped on the pads. The players appeal in unison but the umpire stays put. Rabada is quite not sure as he points out the fact that it might be going down leg. Faf du Plessis still goes for the review. Replays show that there was no bat involved. Ball Tracker shows that the ball was pitched outside leg which means the umpires decision stands and South Africa have lost one review.
Jeet Raval has been caught leg before by Kagiso Rabada. The original decision is not out but Faf du Plessis has decided to review it. Looks to be angling down leg to the naked eye.

Drinks time! A riveting first hour of Test cricket here at the Reserve. South Africa are right on top of things as they've bagged three wickets, one of them of the big gun Kane Williamson, and kept the home side to just 32 runs. The Protea pacers, all three of them, have been right on the money and got the desired results. Jeet Raval has looked comfortable amidst all the mayhem and been patient. He is the key to New Zealand recovering from here. A vital hour of play for them now.
Angling in on the stumps, it's nudged down to fine leg for a single.

Leading edge for Raval but it's in the gap. Philander switches the angle and comes from around the wicket, angles in a length delivery from around off, Jeet closes the face too early and gets a leading edge past point for a double.
Swinging back in on middle and leg, it's turned to the on side for a single.
Keeps it around that off stump channel, hurls it on a length as Henry meets it with the full face.
Closer to the off stick, Nicholls reaches out to play and gets an edge through point. Two runs are taken.
Harmles length delivery well outside off, no trouble for Henry Nicholls to leave it alone.
FOUR! Terrific shot, beautiful timing. Fractionally straight from Rabada once more, Raval is onto it in a flash. Turns this through backward square leg and picks up another boundary.
A bit too straight, on leg, it goes off the pads and rolls fine down the leg side. A leg bye is taken.
Henry Nicholls is the next man in.

OUT! Rabada with another one! But what a catch, Quinton de Kock. Sensational stuff from the Protea keeper. Kagiso with a brilliant length delivery on off, it shapes away at the last second and forces Neil Broom to play at it. He has to stick his bat out, ends up getting an edge which flies behind. Quinton de Kock dives full stretch to his right, dives low and takes it with one hand. Not the ideal debut Neil Broom would have liked. But a stunner of a catch which sees South Africa clearly on top of this game right now.
Brings out the short one and hits the deck hard, it's angling down leg as Broom ducks to evade.
Back of a length outside off, Broom leaves it be.
Good length delivery outside off, pretty close to the off stump as Neil Broom looks to play it inside the line. Is beaten though as the ball goes past the outside edge.

FOUR! And his patience has paid off. Shot of the morning so far. A bit of a loosener, full and outside off, Raval leans into the drive and caresses it through extra cover for a boundary. The timing is good and the chasing fielder has no chance of stopping that.
Outside off, a watchful leave. He's doing well here, being patient and showing the attributes needed to stick around.
Prods forward to this length delivery, brings his bat ahead of his front pad and meets it with the full face.
In the channel outside off, on a length, no shot attempted by Jeet.
Back of a length delivery around off, defended by Raval off the back foot.

FOUR! Length delivery swinging away from around off, Jeet Raval hangs his bat out and gets a big edge. Flies past the gully fielder and is racing away to the fence. Dean Elgar from third slip tries chasing it down, puts in a dive to parry it back in but instead sends it across the rope.
Debutant Neil Broom makes his way out to the middle.

OUT! WILLIAMSON DEPARTS! That's a big, big wicket for the Proteas. The Kiwi juggernaut has been dismissed early as South Africa celebrate. A vital moment in the hosts' innings and they're in early trouble here. Rabada with a length delivery around off, it's swinging back in heavily as Williamson tries to meet it with a straight bat. Is beaten completely by the inswing as the ball goes past the inside edge and raps him on the back pad. South Africa go up in union and the umpire raises his finger. The kiwi skipper consults his partner and decides to review it. Since there is no Ball Tracking, the third umpire does not have any conclusive evidence to overturn the on-field umpire's call and so, the decision stays. New Zealand in some real trouble here.
Williamson has gone upstairs to review an LBW decision which was given out against him. It seems out to the naked eye and the skipper too hesitated a bit before taking it.
Another one outside off as Kane Williamson watches it go into Quinton de Kock's hands.
Shoots off the deck on a back of a length, well outside off, left alone.
Length delivery aiming the top of off stump, it's blocked out from within the crease in front of covers.
Good leave from Kane. He usually gets out in this fashion but is quite careful this time around. It's jagging back in on a length, some extra bounce off the deck, he drops his wrists to let it be.
Starts off with a length delivery just around off, Williamson is half-forward and blocks it out.
Kagiso Rabada is introduced into the attack.
Another one outside off and it's carefully left alone by Jeet Raval.
Speared in full, the inswinging delivery on middle and leg, Raval flicks it away hard but find the mid-wicket fielder.

Prodigious movement there. Good judgement on Raval's part as well to see it go behind. Shaping away from around off, no shot is offered to it. This is good batting from him, he's being patient and seeing the swinging ball out in this early period.
Disciplined stuff from Philander. He serves it on a length across the left-hander, it's not bothered with.
Length delivery around off, played to point by Jeet. Dot ball.
Some movement in the air and it's hurled on a length, outside off, comes back in as Raval leaves it alone.
He's off the mark. Kane Williamson flicks this through the square leg region and picks up a couple of runs for doing so.

Quite full on middle and leg, it's angling in at first but then straightens up a touch as Williamson closes the face to flick. It takes the leading edge but fortunately for the Kiwi skipper, rolls along the ground a bit square on the off side.
Excellent line. The ball doesn't move much either. Just outside off, goes on straight as Williamson plays this inside the line. Is beaten past the outside edge as the keeper behind collects it.

Morne Morkel is having some problem in his run-up. Some sawdust has been called for by the umpire, it's being sprinkled around the area where the bowler lands his foot right before releasing the ball from his hand.
Rock solid in defense, is Kane Williamson. He stands his ground and meets this fuller ball with the full face of the bat.
Skipper Kane Williamson will bat at number 3. Again he walks out on a stage where New Zealand have lost and early wicket and the onus lies on him to lead the side from the front.

OUT! MORKEL STRIKES! And South Africa are away. Beautiful from Morne Morkel. Bowls it on a back of a length, on off, Latham has no choice but to play at it. Gets a thick outside edge and it flies behind to Dean Elgar at third slip who moves to his left to take it. New Zealand down a wicket early in this game.
Sharp from Morkel. He's getting some good bounce off the track. It decks back in on a back of a length, strikes Latham on the thigh pad as he tries to play at it.
Serves this well outside off, an easy leave for the batsman and that will be the end of the over.
Philander loudly appeals but that was always going down leg. Coming back in on a fuller length, Latham is caught low on the pads as he looks to flick but misses. A leg bye is taken.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
In the off stump channel on a good length, it's left alone for the keeper to collect.
Too straight as it's fired in full on the pads, Raval flicks it through backward square leg for a single.

OH MY WORD! How close was that??? Jeet Raval is a brave man, to say the least. Wow! That's just missed. Excellent length delivery from Vernon Philander as it's pitched just around off, it's swinging back in as Raval lunges forward to defend. The ball literally just misses the off stump by centimeters. Really close call.
Tom Latham has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Fuller length delivery outside off, lovely timing from Latham as he drives it through the cover region for a couple.

BIG, BIG SHOUT FOR A LEG BEFORE! The umpire has said no but that's really close. Oh, boy.. That is close. Morkel thinks of taking the review but his skipper decides against it. Hurls it on a good length on middle and off, at 136 kph, Tom Latham is forward in defense but is rapped on the front pad. Morkel turns and appeals loudly, as do the players in the slip cordon. They think long and hard, Morkel tells his skipper he thinks he's got his man but Faf says no, he thinks height could be an issue. But when he looks at the replays later, he's going to be disappointed. They show the ball to be hitting the stumps. Latham would have been gone, but he survives.

FOUR! EDGED AND AWAY! First boundary of the day for the Black Caps. Although it's come in a rather streaky manner. Excellent length delivery on off, Latham hangs his bat out to it and gets an edge which flies between the slip cordon and gully, away to the third man fence for a boundary.
At 135.7 kph, it's around off on a back of a length, Latham with a confident block off the back foot.
Morne Morkel using the angle and going across the batsman, bowls it around off, Latham with an open face dabs it towards backward point.
On middle and off, Raval plays it back down the track.
Back of a length outside off, Raval stands tall and with a straight bat, blocks it in front of covers.
It's pitched a bit further outside off, Raval is happy to let it be.
This time Philander gets it to go away from the batsman, Raval still makes a leave.

Ripper! What a ball. Vernon Philander has got his radar right instantly. On a back of a length, around off, swings back in as Raval makes a leave. That just about whiskered past the off stump. A little too close for comfort.
Too straight from Philander, it's coming back in on middle and leg, goes off the thigh pad as Latham looks to flick and a leg bye is taken.
On a good length from Morkel, around off, Jeet with a solid front foot defensive shot. Ends the over in solid fashion.
Not much swing on this occasion, Raval turns this just wide of mid on for no run.

PEACH OF A DELIVERY! Wonderful, wonderful stuff from Morne Morkel. Bowls this on a brilliant length, moving away just around off, Raval looks to play this from inside the line but is just beaten past the outside edge.
In the channel outside off, Raval sees the bounce from the deck and ensures he has nothing to do with that.
Pitched slightly ahead of a length, around off, Raval comes half-forward and blocks it out.
Shaping away from around off, on a good length, Jeet Raval makes a watchful leave.
Once again stays right behind the line of this one and blocks to end the over.
First runs of the day for New Zealand! Lovely looking shot from Tom Latham. He leans forward to this full delivery and drives it back down the ground past mid on for a couple of runs.
Beautiful! On a good length and just outside off, nipping back in, Latham covers the line well, plants his front foot forward and gracefully shoulders his arms to let it through.
Length delivery just around the off pole, Tom Latham stays right behind the line and keeps it out with a straight blade.
Spills this down the leg side, Latham tries tickling it fine down the leg side but misses.

Philander immediately attacking Tom Latham here. Bowls a length ball on middle and leg, raps Latham on the thigh pad as he tries to flick it away. There's a muted appeal for a leg before but it's going down leg.
Vernon Philander will share the new ball with Morne Morkel from the other end.
Tailing back in slightly on middle and leg, worked in front of Stephen Cook at short leg and that will be the end of the over.
Some sharp bounce for Morkel. Pounds it on a back of a length, climbs on Raval a little too quickly as he fends it away. Goes off the shoulder of the bat in front of gully.
Morne Morkel gets this to move away from Raval, he does well to stand tall and let it be. Isn't taking any chances.
Keeps it on the shorter side and bangs it in around off, it's defended solidly off the back foot.
Slanting away on a back of a length, from around off, it's left alone once again by Raval.
Morkel starts off with an excellent back of a length delivery outside off, Jeet Raval watches the ball closely as he shoulders his arms to it.

We are all set to get things underway here at the Basin Reserve with the players and the umpires making their way out into the middle. Jeet Raval and Tom Latham will open the innings for New Zealand with the former taking strike. Morne Morkel to start things off with the ball for the Proteas. Three slips and a gully in place. Here we go...

TEAM NEWS - South Africa have remained unchanged. No reason for them to tinker around right now at least. And, as expected, New Zealand have a few changes. Trent Boult and Ross Taylor miss out through injuries and are replaced by Tim Southee and Neil Broom respectively. Mitchell Santner is another change, most likely because of the conditions, as Colin de Grandhomme comes in place of him.

TOSS - The coin has been spun and it has gone the visitors' way. SOUTH AFRICA WILL BOWL FIRST! No surprise there, really. Easy decision for Faf du Plessis. Kane Williamson also said he would have bowled first, but mentioned that the wicket has normally been a good one for batting.
The pitch is nice and hard with a nice, green tinge of grass on it. It is suitable for pace bowling. Expect the ball to be swinging about.

WEATHER - Although it is said to keep our fingers crossed when talking about the weather in New Zealand, the forecast for the five days is said to to be a good one for cricket. And right now, as I write this down, it is bright and sunny out there.

As far as the team news is concerned, New Zealand are in a spot of bother. They will be without Trent Boult and Ross Taylor who have been ruled out of this Test due to injuries. Remains to be seen how the Kiwis deal with this situation.

This time, however, we can hope that we have a much better outcome. Wellington is overcast, but the weather is relatively better. The first half of the day could see some showers, but the latter part is forecast to be bathed in sunshine. Let's keep our fingers crossed.

After having the final day washed out in Dunedin, we now make out way to Wellington where both teams will face off in an attempt to take that all-important lead in this 3-match Test series. Two teams are in sublime form and have producing some good contests, right through the ODI series. The Test series opener unfortunately saw a super battle wash away.
